subject: Throughput degradation audit + compensation allocation discussion
messages:
--- Message 1 of 5 ---
From: Samir Shah <ops@fastcart.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 23:12:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden throughput drop on prod-usw2 (10 Aug ~22:40-23:10 UTC)

Hi Mina,

We're seeing a ~40% reduction in successful inference throughput against the Redwood endpoint for our checkout flow between ~22:40 and 23:10 UTC yesterday. Latency per request also spiked briefly (~600ms p95 -> ~1.8s). We attached our sampled request log (request_sample_20280810.csv) and a small chart.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with any infra events on your side? Our customers hit retries and a few orders timed out.

We need:
- confirmation of the exact window and a short summary of root cause (if available) for our legal/ops team
- an estimate of credit eligibility under our SLA if this is a Redwood service issue

Thanks,
Samir
Ops Lead, FastCart

--- Forwarded attachment: request_sample_20280810.csv (3 KB) ---

--- Message 2 of 5 ---
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <ops@fastcart.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Aug 2028 01:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on prod-usw2 (10 Aug ~22:40-23:10 UTC)

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick heads up and the request sample. We're sorry to hear this impacted checkout. I'm looping in Diego (SRE) to pull the telemetry and Laura from Customer Success so we can coordinate communication and any credit discussion.

Initial plan:
- Diego: gather raw traces, autoscaler logs, and eviction/queue metrics for 22:30–23:30 UTC (we'll attach the bundle).
- Laura: catalog customer impact and prepare communication; we'll confirm SLA applicability once we validate the window.
- I'll coordinate and aim to get a first-pass timeline today.

Can you confirm whether FastCart observed an increase in request concurrency or any traffic shape change at the start of the window? That helps us distinguish autoscaler coldstart vs. upstream burst.

—Mina
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 of 5 ---
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <ops@fastcart.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Aug 2028 09:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on prod-usw2 (10 Aug ~22:40-23:10 UTC)

Hi all — I pulled the candidate traces and our autoscaler events. Quick notes:
- Evidence of an autoscaler scale-down + subsequent scale-up during the window. There was a short period where pods were being recreated (22:37:18–22:45:02 UTC).
- Concurrent traffic from FastCart did not show an extraordinary burst in our ingress logs — your sample aligns with normal traffic.
- We also observed increased scheduling latency for the quantized runtime process on a subset of nodes during the warmup period. Stack traces attached as autoscaler_trace_2028-08-10.ndjson and a small diagnostic chart (fastcart_throughput_chart.png).

Preliminary hypothesis: a noisy neighbor/eviction event caused a scale-down reaction followed by a delayed scale-up; during warmup the runtime incurred elevated per-token latency which reduced observed throughput.

Next steps:
1) I'll run a targeted log correlation across all FastCart requests to produce an ordered timeline and a list of affected request IDs.
2) Coordinate with infra to check whether the node eviction was due to capacity pressure or a scheduled maintenance job.
3) Draft a concise RCA; we'll flag whether this meets SLA credit criteria after timeline verification.

Request for FastCart: can you share whether any circuit-breaker/retry policy triggered on your side? That impacts how we apportion failed/slow requests.

—Diego
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

--- Message 4 of 5 ---
From: Samir Shah <ops@fastcart.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@fastcart.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Aug 2028 15:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on prod-usw2 (10 Aug ~22:40-23:10 UTC)

Thanks, Diego. We do see retry spikes and a handful of 504s in our logs; customers reported payment timeouts. We have attached an expanded sample (same CSV with more rows) and a short note from our infra team: they confirm no intentional deployments or scaling on our end at that time.

We'd like to understand: if the event is a Redwood node eviction, is the remedy an SLA credit or a one-time goodwill credit? We are evaluating the revenue impact and will want any remedy reflected against our Q3 invoice.

We appreciate a clear timeline for our finance team so we can process any adjustments.

Samir

--- Attachment forwarded: request_sample_20280810.csv (expanded) ---

--- Message 5 of 5 ---
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <ops@fastcart.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Aug 2028 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on prod-usw2 (10 Aug ~22:40-23:10 UTC)

Samir — thanks for the extra logs and confirmation from your infra team. Quick update and ask:

Confirmed timeline (preliminary):
- 2028-08-10 22:37:18 UTC: node eviction event detected in prod-usw2 (our monitoring).
- 2028-08-10 22:40:00–22:52:00 UTC: scaled-down pool + slower runtime warmup observed; throughput and p95 latency degraded for affected shards.
- 2028-08-10 22:52:30–23:06:00 UTC: scale-up completed and runtime warmed; performance returned to baseline.

What we will deliver by EOD Mon:
- Full ordered timeline with request IDs and mapping to your sample rows (Diego).
- Raw trace bundle and a short RCA with root cause attribution (node eviction due to capacity pressure on mixed workloads) and mitigations (Aditya will propose scheduler-level guardrails).
- A preliminary credit evaluation: based on the timeline and our SLA terms, incidents caused by internal evictions that result in an availability delta are eligible for service credit. Laura will follow up with the finance/CS credit recommendation and options (SLA credit vs. invoice adjustment).

Please confirm if FastCart requires a formal postmortem meeting (we can schedule a 30-minute bridge early next week) and whether you'd like the remediation proposal shared ahead of the meeting.

Also linking the workspace artifacts for your reference: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fastcart-logs and JIRA ticket JIRA-INV-1987.

Thanks again — we will keep this tightly scoped and aim to minimize impact recurrence.

—Mina
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
